The verb かためる means to solidify, harden, or strengthen, and its correct kanji is 固.
default.q.test-9-q8-8.explanation: The verb 固める (かためる, Group 2 transitive verb) literally means “to solidify” or “to make firm,” as with food, jelly, soil, or rocks. Figuratively, it can mean “to strengthen” or “to solidify,” as with one’s resolve or position. It commonly takes を and is in the て-form here to show a sequence of actions. The complete sentence translates as: “Please chill this confection in the refrigerator until it hardens, then enjoy it.” A similar example is: ゼリー液を型に流し込み、冷蔵庫で冷やして固めます (Pour the jelly mixture into a mold, chill it in the refrigerator, and let it set.) To distinguish similar kanji containing 囗, remember that 固 has 口 inside, suggesting something enclosed and solid, unlike 困, which contains 木 and represents a tree trapped in a difficult situation, or 囲, which contains 井 and means to surround.
